item.title: Iran launches drone strikes on Haifa refinery in second attack in three days
item.description:
Iran's military announced Tuesday that it launched drone strikes against Israel's oil and gas refinery and fuel storage facilities in the northern port city of Haifa, marking the second Iranian attack on the facility in three days and a deepening of the energy infrastructure war between the two countries.

"Iran's Army Air Force launched suicide drones targeting oil, gas, and fuel storage facilities of the Israeli regime in Haifa in response to attacks on Iran's oil depots," the spokesman for the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, the unified command of Iran's armed forces, said in a statement carried by Iranian state media. The Haifa refinery, operated by the Bazan Group, is Israel's largest oil-processing facility, with a capacity of 197,000 barrels per day. It had reportedly shut down several units last week as a precautionary measure.

item.title: Merz calls Israel's West Bank settlement push a 'big mistake'
item.description:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Tuesday sharply criticized Israel's settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank, describing the moves as "annexation steps" and calling on the Israeli government to reverse course. Speaking at a joint press conference with Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš in Berlin, Merz warned that advancing the so-called E1 settlement project would "further complicate the two-state solution."

"I want to be clear here," Merz said. "The annexation steps discussed in Jerusalem will further complicate the two-state solution." He added that the German government "urgently demands the abandonment of such steps" regarding the E1 area, calling the project "a big mistake."

item.title: Jurists accuse Bukele's government of crimes against humanity
item.description:
A group of international legal experts filed a formal complaint with the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights on Tuesday, accusing El Salvador's government of committing crimes against humanity during its four-year state of emergency. The 275-page report represents the most serious accusation of human rights violations leveled against President Nayib Bukele's administration since he took office in 2019.

The complaint, filed by the International Group of Experts for the Investigation of Human Rights Violations under the State of Exception in El Salvador — known by its Spanish acronym GIPES — alleges there are "reasonable grounds" to conclude that crimes against humanity, as defined by Article 7 of the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court, are taking place in the Central American nation. The report contends that the violations stem from a state policy "known and even promoted by the highest levels of President Nayib Bukele's government."

item.title: Trial opens for 4 men charged in Haiti president's assassination
item.description: Prosecutors told a Miami jury on Tuesday that greed, arrogance, and a thirst for power drove four men to conspire in the 2021 assassination of Haiti's last democratically elected president, Jovenel Moïse, in a case that has taken nearly five years to reach trial.

item.title: IEA proposes largest-ever oil reserve release amid Hormuz crisis
item.description:
The International Energy Agency has proposed the largest emergency release of oil reserves in its history, surpassing the 182 million barrels released in two batches during the Russia-Ukraine conflict in 2022, as disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz threaten to upend global energy markets. The proposal, first reported by The Wall Street Journal, was circulated during an extraordinary meeting of IEA member governments on Tuesday, with countries expected to decide by Wednesday — and adoption assured unless even one member objects.

The move comes as the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, which began with joint strikes on February 28 under Operation Epic Fury, has effectively shut down the world's most critical oil chokepoint. Commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — which normally carries roughly 20% of global waterborne crude — has ground to a near halt, with maritime intelligence firm Windward reporting just two outbound Iranian-flagged transits and no inbound crossings on March 8.

item.title: IEA to hold emergency meeting as Iran war roils energy markets
item.description: The U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, now in its eleventh day, has upended global energy markets and reignited debate over whether the world's dependence on fossil fuels can survive another geopolitical shock. With oil prices surging more than 24% and roughly 20% of global crude and natural gas supply suspended, some experts and world leaders say the crisis makes the strongest case yet for accelerating the transition to renewable energy — while skeptics warn the moment may pass as quickly as it arrived.

item.title: New AI tools compress months of drug and protein research into days
item.description: A wave of new artificial intelligence tools is reshaping how scientists study gene regulation, decode protein structures, and synthesize drugs, with several studies published in recent weeks demonstrating that machine learning can compress years of laboratory work into days.

item.title: Gold edges higher ahead of key CPI release amid Iran war
item.description: Gold prices rose in early trading on Wednesday as investors balanced ongoing geopolitical risks from the U.S.-Iran war against anticipation of a key inflation report due later in the day. The precious metal climbed to around $5,205 per troy ounce on March 11, gaining 0.31% from the previous session, according to Trading Economics.

item.title: Asian stocks rally as IEA mulls record oil reserve release
item.description: Global stock markets lurched through another volatile stretch as investors grappled with conflicting signals about the trajectory of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, now in its 11th day. Asian equities extended gains on Wednesday while oil prices stabilized after reports that the International Energy Agency was considering a record release of emergency crude reserves.

item.title: Spanish researchers develop artificial cornea from fish scales
item.description: Scientists at Spain's University of Granada have developed an artificial cornea made from fish scales commonly found at local markets, offering what could become a cheaper alternative to donor transplants for patients with severe corneal disease.

item.title: UN Security Council to vote on resolution demanding Iran halt Gulf attacks
item.description: The United Nations Security Council is set to vote Wednesday on a Gulf-backed resolution demanding Iran immediately halt its attacks on neighboring states and cease interference with shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, as Tehran's 11-day campaign of strikes on oil infrastructure and commercial vessels has thrown global energy markets into turmoil.

item.title: Study finds AI weather models use 21 times less energy than traditional systems
item.description: A pair of developments this week highlight how artificial intelligence is reshaping weather prediction — not only by making it more accessible, but by making it far less energy-intensive. Researchers at the University of California San Diego unveiled Zephyrus, the first AI agent designed to let users query weather and climate data in plain language, while a separate study published in the journal Weather found that AI-driven forecasting models consume at least 21 times less energy than their traditional counterparts over one year of operation.

item.title: Anthropic launches policy institute amid Pentagon legal battle
item.description: Anthropic on Tuesday announced the creation of the Anthropic Institute, a new research body focused on studying the societal impacts of increasingly powerful AI systems, even as the company wages a legal fight against the Pentagon over its designation as a national security risk.

item.title: Three commercial ships hit by projectiles in Strait of Hormuz attacks
item.description: At least three commercial vessels were struck by unknown projectiles in and around the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, in the most serious escalation of maritime attacks in the waterway since the U.S.-Israel-Iran conflict began nearly two weeks ago.

item.title: Meta rebuked over AI war fakes reaching millions
item.description: A wave of AI-generated fake videos, images, and fabricated satellite imagery tied to the U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran has reached hundreds of millions of views across social media, prompting platform crackdowns, an advisory board rebuke of Meta, and growing unease among technology investors with stakes in the Middle East.

item.title: G7 backs IEA's largest-ever oil reserve release amid Iran war
item.description:
The International Energy Agency has proposed releasing up to 400 million barrels from emergency oil stockpiles — the largest coordinated drawdown in the agency's 52-year history — as crude prices remain volatile amid the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, according to a report first published by The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday.

The proposal, circulated during an emergency meeting of energy officials from the IEA's 32 member nations on Tuesday, March 10, would more than double the previous record of 182 million barrels released in two rounds in 2022 following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. A decision is expected on Wednesday, with the plan set to be adopted unless any member country raises an objection.

item.title: IEA confirms largest-ever oil reserve release at 400M barrels
item.description:
The International Energy Agency on Wednesday confirmed it will release 400 million barrels of oil from emergency stockpiles, the largest coordinated intervention in the agency's 52-year history, as governments scramble to contain an energy crisis triggered by the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran.

"The oil market challenges we are facing are unprecedented in scale," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said in a statement. "IEA member countries have responded with an emergency collective action of unprecedented size."

The decision, announced at 1300 GMT, came ahead of a virtual meeting of Group of Seven leaders chaired by French President Emmanuel Macron to finalize details of the coordinated response. The release more than doubles the previous record of 182 million barrels that IEA member nations distributed in 2022 following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: Iran's president's son says new leader is 'safe and sound' amid injury reports
item.description:
Iran's newly appointed Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has not appeared publicly, issued a video address, or released a written statement since the Assembly of Experts declared him the country's third supreme leader on March 9, raising mounting questions about his condition amid an ongoing war with the United States and Israel.

Three Iranian officials told The New York Times that Khamenei, 56, sustained injuries including to his legs during the opening day of the U.S.-Israeli military operation on February 28 — the same strikes that killed his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, along with dozens of other senior officials and members of the Khamenei family. The officials said the new leader "was alert and sheltering at a highly secure location with limited communication".

item.title: Von der Leyen calls return to Russian energy 'a strategic blunder' amid Iran war
item.description:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen told the European Parliament on Tuesday that turning back to Russian fossil fuels to ease the energy shock from the Iran war would be "a strategic blunder," even as she acknowledged the conflict has already cost European taxpayers €3 billion in extra energy import costs in just 10 days.

Speaking in Strasbourg ahead of the European Council summit scheduled for March 19-20, von der Leyen laid out the scale of the damage: gas prices have risen 50% and oil prices 27% since the U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran began on February 28. "This is the price of our dependency," she said, while insisting that the EU's diversification efforts since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine have left Europe better prepared than before.

item.title: Markets whipsaw as Iran war escalates and CPI data lands
item.description:
Global markets swung between gains and losses on Wednesday as investors navigated an intensifying military conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran alongside fresh consumer inflation data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

The February Consumer Price Index report, released Wednesday morning, covers a period before the U.S.-Iran war broke out on February 28 and was widely expected to show headline inflation holding steady at 2.4% year over year, with a 0.3% monthly increase, according to FactSet estimates cited by Morningstar. Core CPI, which strips out food and energy, was forecast at 0.3% monthly and 2.5% annually. Analysts noted the data would offer limited insight into the economic fallout from the conflict. "This data is from before the recent conflict in the Middle East broke out, so it's not going to give us a whole lot of information on how prices are starting to respond to that," said Josh Jamner, senior investment strategy analyst at ClearBridge, adding that energy price effects would be "a March and April dynamic".
